raw_response:
I have been growing cotton here in Quzhou for 45 years. My land is 7 mu, all cotton, and I do what has worked for me and what my neighbors do. Let me think through this season.

For seed, I buy Bt hybrid cotton seed every year now — everyone around here does. The bollworm used to destroy us before Bt, so I do not go back to old seed. One bag covers my 7 mu with some to spare.

For fertilizer, I base on what I used last year. I put down compound fertilizer (diammonium and potassium chloride mixed) before planting as base fertilizer, then topdress urea at squaring and again at flowering. For my 7 mu I usually buy about 2 bags of diammonium phosphate (50 kg each) as base, plus 2 bags of urea for topdressing, and 1 bag of potassium chloride. That works out to around 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, and about 8 kg potassium. Cotton eats a lot of potassium or the bolls do not fill — my neighbor learned this the hard way.

I would rather put a little extra urea than come up short. Fertilizer costs money but a poor harvest costs more.

Irrigation: I have well water, so I water before planting to get a good stand, then once at squaring, once at flowering, once at boll-filling if it is dry. Usually 4 times total.

Pesticide: cotton is the worst for pests. Even with Bt seed I still spray for aphids, spider mites, and lygus bugs. I spray about 7-8 times through the season. I watch my neighbors' fields — if they spray, I spray.

Tillage: I plough deep every 2-3 years, rotary in between. This year I will rotary since I ploughed last fall.

Yield target: in a normal year I get around 280 kg seed cotton per mu. Good years 320, bad years 230.
